variants.title: Worn
variants.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: LCL game art-direction comparison, one complete landscape image. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET, Opaque Signal. Preserve its fixed elevated three-quarter oblique/trimetric near-parallel game camera, full landscape framing, continuous playable stone floor, five human figures in their exact positions and poses (four waiting bowl holders and a technician at far right), four dispensing trays and bowls, machine wall footprint, cream pipe with coral collars, left shelving and bench, piers, rear stairs and gallery, right tool cart. Preserve opaque painted brushwork and readable modeled forms rather than photorealism. This is a controlled edit of the SAME SCENE. No added figures, no missing trays, no cinematic perspective, no horizon, no floating diorama. No title or watermark. Primary request: push GRIT WITH A HISTORY forcefully. Make material wear distinct and placed by use: greasy dark hand marks around service controls; soot on stone above lanterns and warm exhaust; rubbed polished walking lanes against rough dark edges; cream enamel cracked or worn only at service access edges, careful fitted repair plates and deliberately maintained moving parts. Clothing has weight, creases, hand-stitched patches and contrasting fabric repairs. Coarse dry opaque brushwork in deep charcoal shadows, a few strongly drawn sharp edges on hands and mechanisms. Increase dramatic dark-light separation while preserving warm amber task light and modest coral signal bands. Machines are functioning, people skilled; avoid generalized rusty wreckage, debris heaps, rain, fog or arbitrary clutter. Desired feel: tactile, heavy, severe, inhabited, visually vigorous.
variants.observations: Five people, four trays/bowls and main hall/camera anchors retained. Rougher stone/floor, chipped enamel, dark handprints around access panels and stitched apparel patches are visible. Wear spreads over broad floor and pier surfaces, so the requested selective use-history becomes partially generalized distress. Some handprints are literal repeated motifs. Service hardware stays functioning; fine repair-plate and fabric design changed. Warm amber pools/green states retained. No added narrative event.

Green machine state lenses changed to amber; light/palette comparison is not controlled. Vent design, fine fittings and apparent sheen differ.

Bay markings sit beside rather than consistently above openings. Cards cover peripheral floor/gallery, not figures or trays. This is a raster UI hypothesis, no implemented game interface or confirmed allocation mechanic.

Preserve opaque painted brushwork and readable modeled forms rather than photorealism. This is a controlled edit of the SAME SCENE. No added figures, no missing trays, no cinematic perspective, no horizon, no floating diorama. No title or watermark. Primary request: overlay HUMAN ORNAMENT as a second visual style within material objects, boldly enough to read at this camera distance. Keep automated machinery geometrically disciplined, existing architecture, light and opaque painting intact. Add a coherent original family of curving leaf-and-loop shapes made by people: richly embroidered broad coat hem and shoulder borders on the existing waiting figures, a neatly fitted patterned cloth runner on the existing left bench, hand-painted glazed bands on existing bowls, and one cared-for cloth wrap on the technician's existing tool-cart handle. Give these motifs a flatter decorative folk-print treatment inside the modeled painted world, with muted petrol blue, coral, ochre and warm ivory, more colour confidence than base but still moody. Skilled visibly intentional decoration and cloth repairs; no litter, extra props, extra people, huge tapestries, costumes or fantasy runes. Palette and patterned silhouettes should be immediately distinguishable from the original at thumbnail size. Warm ordinary beauty and a sense of distinct local culture. No UI or text.
variants.observations: Five people, four trays/bowls and main hall/camera anchors retained. Broad embroidered hems/shoulders, patterned bowls, bench textile and cart cloth create a distinct flat leaf-and-loop decorative layer in coral/ochre/petrol. Ornament also spread onto pipe and machine fascia despite the requested focus on human belongings, and the cart gained a broad cloth rather than only a handle wrap. This compares a more extensively decorated community scene, not a clean separation between human objects and untouched machinery. Motifs and cultural meaning remain proposals.

user_direction: Opaque still better, but the direction remains unresolved. Seek more impact through grit, beauty or a contrasting visual layer. Explore the four proposed branches.
authority: User authorized exploration, not final aesthetic approval or new canon.
